name: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with hypodiploidy
aliases: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia with hypodiploidy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of B-lymphoblasts expressing CD19, CD10, and TdT by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry
Detection of hypodiploid karyotype with fewer than 44 chromosomes in leukemic cells
Bone marrow biopsy showing ≥20% lymphoblast infiltration
Clinical features consistent with acute leukemia such as anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of B-lymphoblast immunophenotype with confirmed hypodiploid karyotype and ≥20% bone marrow lymphoblast infiltration
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Hypodiploidy is a poor prognostic marker and should be confirmed by cytogenetic or molecular methods.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked lymphoblast proliferation in bone marrow
pathognomonic.notes: Identified by bone marrow biopsy and flow cytometry
searchTerms: large number of immature lymphocytes in marrow

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypodiploid karyotype (<44 chromosomes) in leukemic cells

searchTerms: pale skin and tiredness from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low red blood cells

common.symptomName: Thrombocytopenia leading to petechiae and easy bruising
searchTerms: easy bruising and small red spots
high white blood cell count with blasts
increased abnormal white cells in blood

common.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to infiltration

occasional.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to leukemic infiltration

occasional.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement symptoms (e.g., headache, cranial nerve palsies)
searchTerms: headache and nerve palsies from CNS disease
neurological symptoms like cranial nerve weakness

rare.notes: Due to marrow failure or DIC

laboratory: Bone marrow biopsy with >20% lymphoblast infiltration
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT may show mediastinal mass
Ultrasound for hepatosplenomegaly and testicular involvement
MRI brain/spine if CNS involvement suspected
genetic: Absence of common B-ALL translocations (e.g., BCR-ABL1)
Possible TP53 mutations associated with hypodiploidy
other: CSF analysis if CNS involvement suspected

redFlags: Central nervous system symptoms indicating leukemic infiltration
Poor response to initial chemotherapy associated with hypodiploidy
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 5th Edition, 2017
Pui CH, et al. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Lancet. 2012;379(9817):1502-1513.
Moorman AV, et al. Prognostic impact of hypodiploidy in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Blood. 2010;115(9):1871-1878.
